_comment: Plugin manifest (authored by the plugin author). 'version' is the plugin semver (release-only); install-plugin reads 'setup'.
name: autocode
description: Run a project's primary session as an autocode agent under OpenCode 2: autocode.rule.md (always-on, dormant in a session that is not an autocode agent) maps what the persona ties to harness hooks and the session clock onto autocode's wakes, checks, messages, jobs and compaction; autocode-start.skill.md starts such a session (register, read-first by hand, the schedule as wakes, the guard); tools/guard.py is the idle guard's check (open work, and background jobs that are watched: lost at a reboot, past their deadline, their wake not fired); tools/wakes.py prints wake specs from <pack>/.memory/schedule.json.

optional.name: resource-sharing
optional.why: ask a fleet agent for GPU hosts and hold the per-GPU locks it hands out

notes: Needs OpenCode 2.3.0 or later with the plugin of autocode 1.1.0-rc1 or later connected to an autocode server (autocode_me action=status answers; an older OpenCode is refused, and the tools say so). Whole-session costs need autocode 1.1.0-rc3, and coming back by itself after a reboot needs 1.1.0-rc2. From 1.1.0-rc4 a new session cannot take an agent ID that is registered: the owner moves an agent to a new session (autocode agents register ID --session SES).

Best run on the autocode server's own machine, in OpenCode's background service: there the session comes back by itself after a restart of OpenCode, a reboot or a power cut. On another machine the owner opens OpenCode after a reboot, and the session needs a wake of 30 minutes or less without a check to keep its folder loaded.

The owner sets the compaction threshold per ID pattern on the server (autocode settings set compact_at <tokens> --match '<pattern>'); attaching this plugin turns Solaris self-compaction off for the project (only the project's own selfcompact.enabled turns it back on).

Start the session with autocode-start.skill.md; it records the session's agent ID and start prompt under an 'Autocode' heading in <pack>/instructions.md at the first start. tools/guard.py keeps its state in <pack>/.memory/guard/ (private, like the rest of <pack>/.memory/).
